    13  /-!
    14  # Lie algebras of associative algebras
    15  
    16  This file defines the Lie algebra structure that arises on an associative algebra via the ring
    17  commutator.
    18  
    19  Since the linear endomorphisms of a Lie algebra form an associative algebra, one can define the
    20  adjoint action as a morphism of Lie algebras from a Lie algebra to its linear endomorphisms. We
    21  make such a definition in this file.
    22  
    23  ## Main definitions
    24  
    25  * `LieAlgebra.ofAssociativeAlgebra`
    26  * `LieAlgebra.ofAssociativeAlgebraHom`
    27  * `LieModule.toEnd`
    28  * `LieAlgebra.ad`
    29  * `LinearEquiv.lieConj`
    30  * `AlgEquiv.toLieEquiv`
    31  
    32  ## Tags
    33  
    34  lie algebra, ring commutator, adjoint action
    35  -/
    36  
    37  @[expose] public section
    38

    40  universe u v w w₁ w₂
    41  
    42  section OfAssociative
    43  
    44  variable {A : Type v} [Ring A]
    45  
    46  namespace LieRing
    47  
    48  /-- An associative ring gives rise to a Lie ring by taking the bracket to be the ring commutator. -/
    49  @[instance_reducible]
    50  def ofAssociativeRing : LieRing A where
    51    add_lie _ _ _ := by simp only [Ring.lie_def, right_distrib, left_distrib]; abel
    52    lie_add _ _ _ := by simp only [Ring.lie_def, right_distrib, left_distrib]; abel
    53    lie_self := by simp only [Ring.lie_def, forall_const, sub_self]
    54    leibniz_lie _ _ _ := by
    55      simp only [Ring.lie_def, mul_sub_left_distrib, mul_sub_right_distrib, mul_assoc]; abel
    56  
    57  theorem of_associative_ring_bracket (x y : A) : ⁅x, y⁆ = x * y - y * x :=
    58    rfl
    59  
    60  @[simp]
    61  theorem lie_apply {α : Type*} (f g : α → A) (a : α) : ⁅f, g⁆ a = ⁅f a, g a⁆ :=
    62    rfl
    63  
    64  end LieRing
    65  
    66  attribute [local instance 100] LieRing.ofAssociativeRing
    67  
    68  section AssociativeModule
    69  
    70  variable {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    71  
    72  set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
    73  /-- We can regard a module over an associative ring `A` as a Lie ring module over `A` with Lie
    74  bracket equal to its ring commutator.
    75  
    76  Note that this cannot be a global instance because it would create a diamond when `M = A`,
    77  specifically we can build two mathematically-different `bracket A A`s:
    78  1. `@Ring.bracket A _` which says `⁅a, b⁆ = a * b - b * a`
    79  2. `(@LieRingModule.ofAssociativeModule A _ A _ _).toBracket` which says `⁅a, b⁆ = a • b`
    80    (and thus `⁅a, b⁆ = a * b`)
    81  
    82  See note [reducible non-instances] -/
    83  abbrev LieRingModule.ofAssociativeModule : LieRingModule A M where
    84    bracket := (· • ·)
    85    add_lie := add_smul
    86    lie_add := smul_add
    87    leibniz_lie := by simp [LieRing.of_associative_ring_bracket, sub_smul, mul_smul, sub_add_cancel]
    88  
    89  attribute [local instance] LieRingModule.ofAssociativeModule
    90  
    91  theorem lie_eq_smul (a : A) (m : M) : ⁅a, m⁆ = a • m :=
    92    rfl
    93  
    94  end AssociativeModule
